restrictions: Typing was exercised with synthetic key events, not by a person with a real keyboard in the real window: the window was started with GDK_BACKEND=x11 (XWayland) and GDK_CORE_DEVICE_EVENTS=1 and Ctrl+A then M, a, r, i, e were sent to it with XSendEvent; the label then showed "Bonjour Marie" in the capture taken 501-507 ms after the first key was sent (upper bound for the update delay, to be compared with the 1 s of User Story 1). The default GDK backend of this system is Wayland, which was not driven this way; real keyboard input, input methods and the IME path were not tested.

The end-of-life GtkInfoBar was not exercised: the WSL2 kernel 6.18.58.1 is not end of life for the backend, so eol_warning_shown was false in every run and the warning (FR-013, ui-contract item 3) was never displayed on Linux. It stays unverified at run time until a run on a kernel the backend treats as end of life.

Dark theme and high contrast were only forced through GTK_THEME (Adwaita:dark, HighContrast, HighContrastInverse), not through the system settings (gsettings color-scheme, the accessibility high-contrast switch, the Ubuntu Yaru theme): this distribution has only the Default and Emacs themes installed besides the themes built into GTK, and no desktop session of a full distribution was involved (WSLg only). The contrast ratio measured on the captured pixels of the greeting label (WCAG formula, most contrasting pixel against the most frequent colour of the label band) was 11.61 (default), 10.56 (Adwaita:dark), 13.88 (HighContrast) and 11.88 (HighContrastInverse), all above 4.5:1, but the HighContrast theme rendered by GTK 3.24 is mild-looking and is not a proof for the real high-contrast mode of a desktop.

Screenshots are captures of the window client area only (Gdk pixbuf of the X11 window under XWayland, 480x240): no title bar, no window decoration, no desktop, no screen recording. The probe runs use the default (Wayland) backend while the screenshots use the X11 backend, so no screenshot shows the exact process of the timing runs. 'displayed' in the probe record comes from the application's own first draw callback; that the compositor put the pixels on a screen was not independently checked.

Only GTK 3.24.41 was run. The GTK 3.10 API subset is enforced at compile time (GDK_VERSION_MIN_REQUIRED/MAX_ALLOWED = 3.10, no warning), but the executable was never run on a real GTK 3.10, so the lower limit of this UI is not verified here.

Only one environment was exercised: Ubuntu 24.04.5 in WSL2 with WSLg on a Windows 11 host, x86_64. Not tested: bare metal or a full VM boot, other distributions (the Ubuntu 22.04 and other targets of T059 have no record), other desktops, real GPU or software-rendering differences, Linux ARM. The timings and memory figures are those of this WSL2 virtual machine.

Glyph rendering was looked at (glyphs-*.png, viewed by the author of the trial), with the Noto fonts installed in this WSL image, for accents, CJK, emoji (a ZWJ family sequence, a flag, a skin-tone sequence), Hebrew and Arabic, combining marks (Latin, Thai, Devanagari), symbols (currency, arrows, math, box drawing, dingbats) and Latin Extended: the input field and the greeting label draw the same characters. This is a capture of one distribution with one font set (Noto Sans, Noto Sans CJK, Noto Color Emoji): nothing was checked about other font sets, other desktops, or a real person reading the screen. Right-to-left order was looked at only for Hebrew and Arabic in one string. Missing fonts are an environment limit, not a defect of the UI: with only DejaVu, Ubuntu and MathJax fonts (the image before the Noto packages were installed) CJK, Thai, Devanagari and most emoji code points were drawn as hexadecimal boxes in BOTH the input field and the label, identical in the two widgets (glyphs-dejavu-only-*.png); a system without those fonts will always show boxes. The packages that fix it on Ubuntu are fonts-noto-cjk, fonts-noto-color-emoji and fonts-noto-core.

The scrolling of a long greeting was only seen in captures (the first lines are visible and the window keeps 480x240); the scrollbar and the mouse wheel or keyboard scrolling of the greeting area were not exercised. The trial evidence above (probe series, trial-measurements.json, themes, typed Marie, run_vectors log and the window captures window-*.png) was produced with the executable 5bd33f1d… built before the commit that adds the scrolled window (the commit holding this record); only the glyphs-* evidence and a run_vectors run (log not stored: a re-run) were produced with the executable f83a1a13… of the fix, so the timings, memory and theme measurements were not repeated with it.
No procedure document exists yet for this trial (validation/procedures/linux.md is task T111), so the verdict carries no 'reproduction' path; the commands used are in the 'notes' field.

Re-run after adr/0004-fallback-per-case.md (2026-11-13): the executable of the evidence listed before this entry is sha256 5bd33f1d990d01c13c19773523d491f3e0a4f806287133657dba9f81f16c12dd (296848 bytes, libstdc++ and libgcc linked statically); the executable now built links the distribution's libstdc++ and libgcc (meson option static_cxx_runtime, default false) and is sha256 24b62cafff19e3e96cf2d716fd9894a46f7a7e5d75c9407402670d3a36b871cf (53736 bytes, 7 DT_NEEDED entries, highest GLIBC_2.34 and GLIBCXX_3.4.21). RE-VERIFIED on it: 15 of 15 vectors, 10 of the 13 glyph screenshots byte for byte equal to those of the earlier build (accents, cjk, emoji, rtl, combining, symbols, latinext, long, asc250, max1000; the three others have no counterpart), tools/check_std.py (0 failures), ctest with g++ (selftest through <iostream> and Catch2, 2 of 2). NOT re-run: the 20 probe runs, the GUI screenshots in dark and high-contrast themes, the typing. A distribution without a libstdc++.so.6 from GCC 5 or later was not tried; the static variant builds (-Dstatic_cxx_runtime=true, 296952 bytes) but was not run on such a system. The files of this re-run are not stored (CLAUDE.md: evidence is stored only when it proves something new); its results above come from the run logs of 2026-11-13; only the measurement behind the ADR is stored, validation/evidence/adr-0004/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/gtk-floor-and-runtime-check-output.txt.

notes: Environment: WSL2 distribution Ubuntu-24.04 with WSLg, see validation/platforms/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64.json. Commands used (from the repository root, Windows host, Git Bash): 'python tools/build.py linux modern' (build in ~/loomora-build under the distribution home, up to date, no change to the deliverable record), then 20 launches of ~/loomora-build/linux-modern/loomora-gtk3 --probe [--probe-input Marie] with the stdout, stderr, exit status and leftover processes recorded, then 'python tools/run_vectors.py linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64 modern --evidence-dir validation/evidence/<change>/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/', then four runs of the window without --probe, driven by a small Python script (Gdk pixbuf capture of the X11 window, XSendEvent key events, WM_DELETE_WINDOW client message) with GDK_BACKEND=x11, GDK_CORE_DEVICE_EVENTS=1 and GTK_THEME unset, Adwaita:dark, HighContrast, HighContrastInverse. That driver script is not part of the repository. The first run of the '--probe' series was also its slowest (247 ms). The text files of this evidence folder must keep their LF line endings (validation/evidence/.gitattributes marks them -text) because the verdict holds their sha256. Glyph check (2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13): the trial evidence before the commit that adds the scrolled window (the commit holding this record) was produced with the executable of sha256 5bd33f1d, 296,848 bytes. On the image with only DejaVu/Ubuntu/MathJax fonts, CJK, Thai, Devanagari and most emoji showed as hexadecimal boxes in both the field and the label (environment: no font covers them, see glyphs-fonts-coverage.txt); after 'sudo apt install fonts-noto-cjk fonts-noto-color-emoji fonts-noto-core' both widgets draw them identically. One real UI defect was measured with plain ASCII, independent of fonts: a greeting longer than the label area was clipped, blank from 250 characters (glyphs-noto-before-fix-asc250.png) and, with the DejaVu fonts, the window grew from 480x240 to 480x273 at 60 characters (glyphs-dejavu-only-asc60.png). The label now sits in a GtkScrolledWindow (no horizontal scrollbar, automatic vertical one); the executable of sha256 f83a1a130aef05a8cf2d883953bdcc6c4343707525f3268a58abdeb5350cde0c, 296,952 bytes keeps the window at 480x240 and shows the first lines (glyphs-noto-after-fix-asc250.png, -long.png, -max1000.png; the seven other captures of the fixed build are byte-identical to the before-fix ones and are not stored), and 'python tools/run_vectors.py linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64 modern' still passes 15 of 15. The capture script is glyphs-shoot.py; builds for these captures were made in ~/loomora-build-glyphs (same source, same hashes as ~/loomora-build). ADR 0004 (2026-11-13): the earlier evidence was produced with executable 5bd33f1d...c12dd (static C++ runtime); the rebuilt one (24b62caf...71cf, dynamic C++ runtime, same source) was re-verified, see the last restriction; the files of that re-run are not stored (CLAUDE.md), only the measurement behind the ADR is, in validation/evidence/adr-0004/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/.
